title: Revolut Swaps Claude Code for Chinese GLM, Cuts Coding Costs 90%
summary: Revolut moved 2,000 engineers from Claude Code to a self-hosted Chinese GLM 5.3 model, cutting AI coding costs ~90% and reducing coding time 60%.
body_markdown:
AI Model Vendor Switch


# Revolut Swaps Claude Code for Chinese GLM, Cuts Coding Costs 90%


By OpenTools Team


·


November 8, 2026


Revolut has moved roughly 2,000 engineers from Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex to a self‑hosted instance of GLM 5.3, an open‑weight model from Beijing‑based Z.ai, cutting AI‑assisted coding costs by approximately 90%. David Abitbol, who leads AI operations and infrastructure at Revolut, shared the migration story at the AI Engineer conference in New York, detailing how the fintech tuned the model from a "terrible" out‑of‑box experience of 14‑second latency down to 1.6 seconds. The move underscores a growing trend: well‑funded engineering organizations are betting on self‑hosted open‑weight models over per‑seat SaaS subscriptions for AI coding tools.


## The Switch: From Claude Code to GLM 5.3


Revolut has made one of the largest AI model vendor migrations in fintech history, shifting roughly 2,000 engineers from[Anthropic's Claude Code](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/revolut-chinese-models/) and[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's Codex to a self-hosted deployment of[GLM 5](https://opentools.ai/llms/glm-5) .3. The model comes from[Z.ai](https://opentools.ai/organizations/z-ai) , a Beijing-based AI lab, and runs on Revolut's own infrastructure in the United States rather than in China.


David Abitbol, who leads AI operations and infrastructure at the $115 billion fintech, presented the migration at the AI Engineer conference in New York, describing it as a calculated bet on open-weight models.[According to Trending Topics](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/revolut-glm-open-weight-coding-costs/) , the move reflects a broader internal conviction that "the bottleneck for engineering is not necessarily coding" but rather the non-coding overhead that surrounds it.


## The Economics: 90% Cost Reduction


The numbers driving the switch are stark. Revolut's AI coding costs fell to roughly a tenth of their previous spend after the migration, with token pricing now hovering around $0.30 per million tokens,[per Cybernews](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/revolut-chinese-models/) and corroborated by[Dealroom](https://dealroom.co/news/169124-revolut-swaps-claude-code-for-a-chinese-open-weight-model-cutting-its-ai/) .


The entire operation runs on 56[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) B200 GPUs serving all 2,000 engineers simultaneously. For a fintech of Revolut's scale — 80 million customers across 45 markets and reportedly targeting a $200 billion IPO — per-engineer SaaS licensing for AI coding assistants had become a meaningful line item.


- **Pre-migration cost** Full-rate Claude Code and Codex per-seat pricing for ~2,000 engineers


- **Post-migration cost** ~$0.30 per million tokens on self-hosted GLM 5.3 — approximately one-tenth of prior spend


- **Infrastructure** 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs running on[US-based infrastructure](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/revolut-glm-open-weight-coding-costs/) , not China


- **Scale** Serving 2,000 engineers simultaneously across Revolut's global engineering org


## Performance Gains: Tuning Away the 'Terrible'


The migration wasn't plug-and-play. Out-of-[box](https://opentools.ai/organizations/box) inference on[GLM 5](https://opentools.ai/llms/glm-5) .3 was, in Abitbol's own words shared at AI Engineer NYC, "terrible" — time to first token clocked in at roughly 14 seconds. After extensive tuning, Revolut brought that down to 1.6 seconds, a nearly 9x improvement,[as reported by Dealroom](https://dealroom.co/news/169124-revolut-swaps-claude-code-for-a-chinese-open-weight-model-cutting-its-ai/) and[Trending Topics](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/revolut-glm-open-weight-coding-costs/) .


The gains extended well beyond latency. Revolut reported coding time down by roughly 60% and lead time — the full cycle from ticket to merged code — down by approximately 70%. The context window is capped at 256K tokens, a deliberate engineering choice. Abitbol reportedly described long-context as "a scam" for most coding use cases,[per Trending Topics](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/revolut-glm-open-weight-coding-costs/) .


> "The bottleneck for engineering is not necessarily coding."


**David Abitbol** - Head of AI Operations & Infrastructure, Revolut


## Infrastructure: Self-Hosted on US Soil


A recurring question around the migration has been data sovereignty.[GLM 5](https://opentools.ai/llms/glm-5) .3 is an open-weight model from a Beijing-based lab, but Revolut runs public model weights entirely on its own infrastructure in the United States, not in China. Abitbol acknowledged what he called "a lot of stigma" around using Chinese open-weight models at an EU-regulated financial institution,[according to Cybernews](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/revolut-chinese-models/) .


The architecture means Revolut's code never leaves its own GPUs. The model weights are publicly available and run locally — there is no API call to[Z.ai](https://opentools.ai/organizations/z-ai) servers, no data exfiltration to Beijing, and no dependency on a Chinese cloud provider. For a regulated bank operating across 45 markets, that distinction is everything.


## The Tradeoffs: What GLM Can and Can't Do


[GLM 5](https://opentools.ai/llms/glm-5) .3 is not a full replacement for the previous toolchain. The model handles only text-based coding tasks. For image-related work, Revolut routes requests to[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) 's Gemini instead,[Trending Topics notes](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/revolut-glm-open-weight-coding-costs/) . Claude Code and Codex remain available to engineers but are now used sparingly rather than as the default.


This multi-model routing architecture — GLM for text coding, Gemini for images, Claude and Codex as fallbacks — reflects a maturing approach to AI tooling in large engineering organizations. Rather than betting on a single vendor, Revolut has built a tiered system where cost, capability, and latency determine which model handles each request.


## Revolut's AI Journey: A Multi-Vendor Search


The GLM migration didn't happen in a vacuum. Revolut's AI coding journey went through several distinct phases,[as detailed by Trending Topics](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/revolut-glm-open-weight-coding-costs/) and[Dealroom](https://dealroom.co/news/169124-revolut-swaps-claude-code-for-a-chinese-open-weight-model-cutting-its-ai/) .


The engineering team first experimented with[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) 's Gemini for AI-assisted coding, which delivered roughly a 20% reduction in coding time — promising but not transformative. Next came a deployment of Claude Code with per-engineer budgets, an attempt to give every developer access to a top-tier coding model. That approach proved costly while delivering only modest incremental gains over the Gemini baseline.[GLM 5](https://opentools.ai/llms/glm-5) .3 was the third attempt, and the one that stuck: open-weight, self-hosted, and tuned aggressively until the performance matched the economics.


## Beyond Coding: Where the Time Actually Goes


Abitbol used his AI Engineer conference talk to make a broader point about engineering productivity. The real time sinks for Revolut's engineers are not in writing code — they're in "the inboxes, Jira, and Confluence" overhead that surrounds development work,[according to Trending Topics](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/revolut-glm-open-weight-coding-costs/) and[Cybernews](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/revolut-chinese-models/) .


An AI coding assistant, however fast or cheap, only addresses the narrow slice of an engineer's day spent actually typing code. Planning, coordination, documentation, and review consume the bulk of engineering hours. The 60% coding-time reduction is real, but it applies to the fraction of work that was code-generation in the first place. Abitbol's framing suggests Revolut sees the GLM migration not as an endpoint but as one piece of a larger effort to reduce non-coding friction across the engineering org.
